messages.subject: Managing Large Data Objects
parts:
Hi,

I've got an application where I need to load a large data object from a file (using load(file="....")).  My trouble is that I need to update portions of the loaded object depending on user inputs and I'm having trouble getting it to work.  Below is a portion of my code. 

My output needs to show a table that's deep inside this loaded data object (named "allData") and allData needs to be updated before it's displayed.  I tried creating a reactive function that returns the updated allData object, but I keep getting errors when trying to access parts of the allData object.  How should I be approaching this problem?

library(shiny)
library(RCurl)
library(rjson)
library(yaml)
library(digest)
library(XML)

source(file="../getTrended.r")
source(file="../getOvertime.r")
source(file="../getRanked.r")

load(file="../allData.data")



shinyServer(function(input, output) {
       
    dataUpdate = reactive({
        if(input$selectedPanel == "Purchase Metrics"){
            #Update Purchase Metrics
            reportSelection = "purchaseMetrics"
            metricID = list("revenue","orders","units", "cartAdditions", "checkouts")
            dateGranularity = input$dateGranularity
            if(difftime(Sys.time(), as.POSIXlt(allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]]$lastUpdated[[dateGranularity]], origin = "1970-01-01"), units="hours") > 1){
                if(dateGranularity == "week"){
                    dateFrom = as.character(7 * floor(as.numeric(as.Date(as.POSIXlt(allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]]$lastUpdated[[dateGranularity]], origin = "1970-01-01"))-1+4) / 7) + as.Date(1-4, origin = "1970-01-01"))
                }else{
                    dateFrom = as.character(as.Date(as.POSIXlt(allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]]$lastUpdated[[dateGranularity]], origin = "1970-01-01")))
                }
                temp = GetOvertimeReport(
                    userName = userName,
                    sharedSecret = sharedSecret,
                    RSID = input$RSID,
                    dateFrom = dateFrom,
                    dateTo = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                    metricID = metricID,
                    dateGranularity = dateGranularity,
                    dataCenter = dataCenter
                )
                replacementVector = as.character(allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]][[dateGranularity]]$Date) == as.character(temp$Date[[1]])
                if(length(which(replacementVector)) == 0){
                    replacementRow = dim(allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]][[dateGranularity]])[1]
                }else{
                    replacementRow = which(replacementVector)[1]
                }
                oldData = allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]][[dateGranularity]][1:replacementRow-1,]
                allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]][[dateGranularity]] = rbind(oldData, temp)
                allData[[input$RSID]][[reportSelection]]$lastUpdated[[input$dateGranularity]] = Sys.time()
            }

parts: If the overwriting is happening inside the reactive expression, it should be fine. If not... you'd have to explain a little more about how/when the rewriting happens for me to answer definitively. Ideally you would not overwrite sub-objects of a giant object, but simply create new reactive expressions; unless there is a good reason for these things to be glommed together into one giant object, you'll get better performance and more understandable code by just keeping separate things separate.

I've included the data as a global object.  Do any changes I make to that global object in a reactive function show up to all other output functions?  Do I have to use the output of the reactive function, or can I just call it and use the updated global object?

x <- 1
f <- function() {
  x <- 2

f()

x

g <- function() {
  x <<- 3
}
g()
x
# 3

-Winston
